newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends down, then gains slightly on AGA.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends down, then gains slightly on AGA.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures, hit by a late wave of selling, mostly ended lower Wednesday in a very active session, then gained slightly on ACCESS after AGA data showed a modest weekly gas stock draw.
May skidded 5.4 cents to close at $2.06 per million British thermal units, then edged up to the $2.07 area in after-hours trade. June settled 8.7 cents lower at $2.077.

"I think most people were expecting a build, but I don't think much of the number," said one East Coast trader, noting the weekly AGA decline was close to expectations for steady to slightly higher stocks and should have little market impact.

AGA said late Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by seven bcf, slightly below expectations for a slight build. Overall stocks were still 256 bcf, or 45 percent, above year-ago levels. Eastern storage, which dropped last week by two bcf, was still 175 bcf, or almost double, last year.
Traders said the market rallied early today on bullish technical signals after Tuesday's strong close but swiftly sold off on profit taking when upside momentum stalled.
Chart watchers pegged May resistance at $2.21, with support seen at $2.035 and $1.925.

But with May set to go off the board Thursday, technical traders turned their attention to June, where resistance was pegged at $2.33 and support at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.00 area.
With storage still comfortable and more seasonal Midwest and eastern weather expected by the weekend, fundamental traders said further cash gains could be difficult.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices jumped more than 10 cents Wednesday to the $2.15-20 area. Midcontinent pipes gained a similar amount to the $2.05 area. Gas at New York city gate rallied by about 15 cents to the $2.50s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip tumbled 6.3 cents to $2.184. NYMEX said a near record 99,318 Hub contracts traded, up sharply from Tuesday's revised tally of 41,569.

On the KCBT, May finished seven cents lower at $1.95, while deferreds ended down by two to 5.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.6 cents to 11.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 596 lots changed hands, down from Tuesday's total of 782.
KCBT May natgas expires Friday, April 25.
